ISSUE #226 — ACCEPTANCE LEDGER ENTRY 13, one narrow visit. Branch slice-dsh-8810, draft PR #327 on main; adopt every commit.

The ledger openspec/changes/2026-09-09-226-session-resumption/acceptance-ledger-8.8-8.10.md maps every acceptance clause of tasks 8.8 and 8.10 to opened evidence and lists the remaining work as narrow units in dependency order. READ its sections 5 and 6 FIRST. You do exactly ONE entry, verbatim below, and nothing else; section 6 is now ONE numbered dependency order of 24 entries (renumbered by the remediation run; its label map is at the top of section 6). Entries 1-10 have landed.


HOST-SUPPLIED SOURCES. Your seat has no network. The host has retrieved every source this entry names, each at an immutable tag with its commit SHA and the file's SHA-256, into .forge/tasks/sources-entry13/ with a MANIFEST.md. Use ONLY those files; if one you need is missing or its manifest row says it could not be retrieved, record that source as pending and continue with the rest. The "Files it updates" list, the proof and the stop-on-divergence rule below all stand.

YOUR ENTRY, verbatim from section 6:

13. **Retrieve, pin and verify the Apple and env sources.** Added by the
   remediation (third return, finding 1). **Externally owned**: it needs a
   seat or host whose grant reaches the network. Every seat of this change so
   far was refused `curl`, `WebFetch`, `gh api` and the GitHub MCP (`tasks.md`
   2389–2394, 2425–2431). The sources are **retrievable, not impossible**.
   Closes N1's and N3's source-pin predicates (1248–1250, 1284–1286) and
   N4's "applicable source-pin cells" (1304–1305).

   **Sources**, each at an immutable revision (a release tag with its commit
   SHA), with the file's SHA-256 recorded:
   - Apple Libc `gen/FreeBSD/exec.c` and `sys/posix_spawn.c`
     (`apple-oss-distributions/Libc`). The port cites design D10's
     moving-`main` ranges 178–218 and 262–297, and 97–143 and 170–195
     (`composite.rs:2617–2631`; design.md 2953–2960).
   - The env dispatch sources the resolver's rule names
     (`composite.rs:3598–3608`): GNU coreutils `src/env.c` and
     `src/coreutils.c`, Apple's `env/env.c`, uutils `src/bin/coreutils.rs`
     and busybox `libbb/appletlib.c`. The code says `usr.bin/env/env.c`;
     proposal.md 3842 links `apple-oss-distributions/shell_cmds`
     `env/env.c`. The retrieval records which path the pinned revision holds.
   - The Linux kernel's `fs/binfmt_script.c`, which the same doc comment
     cites for `argv[0]`.

   Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063), so every source above
   applies and no Windows source is owed. glibc's `posix/execvpe.c` is cited
   to the fixed 2.42 release and N1/N3 do not name it, so it is outside this
   unit.

   **Files it updates.** The pins go "beside the implementation" (design.md
   2958–2959): the doc comments at `composite.rs` 2329–2331, 2367–2368, 2417,
   2617–2631, 2728, 2817, 3104, 3154–3155 and 3598–3608; the source comments
   at `composite/tests.rs` 2360, 7157, 7476, 7703 and 7799–7800; and
   `composite/tests/native_matrix.rs` 210, 607–608 and 861. A dated evidence
   file goes beside `controller-evidence-2026-09-10.md` in this change's
   directory, with each source, tag, commit, file digest and the exact line
   ranges re-read against the port. A delivery record in `tasks.md` under
   8.8.1.1 and 8.8.2.1 cites it.

   **Proof.** Every ported block's cited range is re-read at the pinned
   revision. Where the port's reading differs from the pinned source, that is
   a production finding, and the unit stops and reports it rather than
   editing the port to match. It comes before entry 14 because it moves
   bytes.

   **Kept separate: an operator scope change.** The operator may instead rule
   that N1 and N3 tick without the pins, as inherited debt recorded in prose.
   That would be a change to 8.8's acceptance, not satisfaction of it. It is
   prepared in entry 23, and it does not replace this entry unless the
   operator says so.

RULES. Stay inside the files your unit names. Tests assert exact reasons and exact values, never is_err(); every new test is shown to bind by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, and you record the failing test name and assertion. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. If your unit says a failure on current production bytes is a production finding, STOP and report it as your result instead of adjusting the test. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Keep the session small: commit when the unit is done.

GATES, crate-scoped: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched. Do not run the exact coverage script or tick any checkbox: those are later units. Record in the ledger's section 6, under your entry, one dated line saying what landed and the commit. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/, extensions/ and docs/decisions/ do not move; 0056 stays proposed; the DSH route stays disabled.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: Framed entry 13 in .forge/tasks/entry13-source-pins.md. Ruled chore: bounded source verification, citation updates and evidence records; behavioral divergence requires stopping, with no production, contract or policy change authorized. All eight supplied files exist and match manifest digests; inaccurate manifest line counts must be remeasured. Wrote only triage artifacts; no implementation, delivery gates, commit or recipe selection.

Entry 13 stopped on a production finding, per its proof rule ('the unit stops and reports it rather than editing the port'). Nothing was edited or committed; the tree is clean at 60227b4e. All eight host sources match their MANIFEST digests. The MANIFEST lines column is wrong; the measured counts are in the record. FINDING P1, the Apple EACCES arm: composite.rs:2732-2733 (step) remembers every Apple EACCES as the denial, and so do the doc comments at 2332-2334 and 2728-2730 and the assertion at composite/tests.rs:7175-7181. At Libc-1752.120.2 (4e34d055), EACCES reaches the default arm: sys/posix_spawn.c 178-193 and gen/FreeBSD/exec.c 273-289 read 'if (stat(bp,&sb) != 0) break;' and remember EACCES only when stat succeeds. A candidate in a PATH directory without search permission is therefore walked past WITHOUT being remembered, and an otherwise empty search ends in ENOENT (posix_spawn.c 195-204, exec.c 293-306). The port reaches this through classify_in's metadata EACCES (composite.rs:3294-3299) -> Passed{denied:true} -> Search::find's 'is not executable by this process' (3069-3072), where native macOS reports NotFound. Selection is unaffected; the exhaustion cause and the error kind differ. No test or matrix cell has a sealed directory as the only or last Apple candidate. A repair means making the Apple arm depend on which question failed (metadata vs access/not-regular), not on the errno alone: production code plus its unit assertion, outside this chore. Other readings found no behavioural divergence but need citation corrections when the entry resumes. The quoted strsep/strlen lines (composite.rs:2618-2620, 2639, 2641) are strchrnul at the pin, with the same token sequence. D10's exec.c ranges do not line up with the pin. The _PATH_DEFPATH attribution at 3153-3155 belongs to _execvpe (exec.c 318-328), not execvP. The env sources (GNU env.c, coreutils.c, Apple env/env.c at the env/env.c path because usr.bin/env/env.c is absent at shell_cmds-329, uutils 0.12.0, busybox 1_36_1) and linux v7.2 binfmt_script.c are consistent with composite.rs:3598-3608. Pending because the files were not supplied: the Darwin headers (PATH_MAX/MAXPATHLEN=1024, _PATH_DEFPATH), uutils src/common/validation.rs (the renaming-symlink refusal) and gnulib progname.c. The full line-by-line reading is in the ignored scratch file .forge/entry13-source-reading-2026-09-23.md. No gates were run because no bytes moved. Needs a ruling: a production-repair unit for P1 before entry 13 resumes.
